A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same research work. Their text, equations, figures, Methods, and supplementary Sections S1–S5 support reliable comparison. The bibliography moves before the supplement in v3; supplementary material remains present.

before.justification: v2 reports original simulations and data analyses, including four imaging applications, estimator validation, and IDEAL optimization results in Figures 3–4 and the supplement.

after.justification: v3 retains the original imaging experiments, simulations, estimator analyses, and IDEAL optimization results, including the supplementary experiments.

M1.justification: The mutual-information estimator, stationary and full Gaussian models, PixelCNN architecture, and IDEAL optimization procedure remain unchanged. Expanded main-text explanations do not introduce new algorithmic components.

E1.justification: Both versions use Gehler-Shi, simulated black holes, CIFAR10, BSCCM, MNIST, and the same Gaussian and one-dimensional simulations. Reconstruction, classification, protein prediction, and encoder-design tasks are retained. Gehler-Shi's more prominent mention in v3 is not new coverage.

E2.justification: Corresponding comparisons retain the same Gaussian/PixelCNN estimators, Bayer/random/learned color filters, telescope configurations, one-lens/four-lens/diffuser encoders, and illumination patterns. Newly cited illumination-design papers are not added experimental comparators.

E3.justification: Methods retain the same splits, preprocessing, noise models, metrics, model configurations, and optimization settings. Details newly emphasized in the application narratives, including simulated shot noise and Gaussian telescope noise, were already documented in v2.

E4.justification: Covariance stabilization, patch-size sensitivity, non-Gaussian data, estimator consistency, low-photon behavior, encoder uncertainty, and task-specific classification analyses are retained. Removing the 'Additional performance metrics' subsection heading does not remove Figure S19 or its results.

E5.justification: Bootstrap confidence intervals, repeated model fits, classification repetitions, and training-time standard deviations remain unchanged. The confidence-interval procedures in Methods and uncertainty displays in the figures are retained.

E6.justification: v3 newly reports approximately 0.1 seconds for the initial stationary Gaussian fit, separately from the approximately 10-second iterative fit already reported in v2 Section S3.5. This adds timing information, not a demonstrated speedup. The imaging-performance plots and supplementary numerical results remain unchanged.

T1.justification: The Gaussian-mixture density and Monte Carlo entropy expressions newly displayed in the main text already appear in v2 Section S1.4. The formal models, assumptions, and derivations in Sections S1, S2, and S5 remain unchanged; the added diffraction-limit discussion is explanatory.

C1.justification: The main contributions remain measurement-based information estimation without ground truth, prediction of performance across four imaging domains, and information-maximizing design through IDEAL. Rewriting the abstract, introduction, and closing summary does not materially change their scope.

C2.justification: v3 develops a more explicit rationale about IDEAL's computation and memory benefits and avoiding vanishing gradients. It also proposes using IDEAL designs as starting points for task-specific refinement, extending v2's suggestion about curating task-relevant training data. Existing task-specific and encoder-uncertainty limitations remain.

D1.justification: The implementation summary distinguishes initial and iterative stationary Gaussian fitting times and removes v2's misleading PixelCNN '100s per patch' wording. Detailed implementation instructions, hyperparameters, software, and code-access information otherwise remain unchanged.

R1.justification: v3 adds Kellman et al. (2019), Horstmeyer et al. (2017), and Ji et al. (2023), while removing Van Aert et al. (2006) and Horstmeyer et al. (2016). The broader positioning against estimation theory, compressed sensing, and end-to-end design remains, including Section S5.

P1.justification: The main text undergoes substantial rewriting, especially the probabilistic formulation, two-point example, model descriptions, application narratives, and Discussion. Model descriptions become a structured list, discussion topics are reordered, references move before the supplement, and author-contribution and funding statements are added.

P2.justification: The figures retain their underlying plots and schematics but receive caption and label edits. Figure 2 changes 'Rayleigh resolution' to 'Diffraction-limited resolution'; Figure 4 replaces 'training' with 'optimization'. Figure 1 placement and surrounding layout change, while supplementary displays are retained.

improvement.justification: v3 makes the probabilistic model, worked two-point calculation, and estimator tradeoffs easier to understand in the main text. Contribution and funding disclosures improve transparency. These are limited gains: the stronger assertions about IDEAL's computational and memory benefits lack new comparative benchmarks, tempering the improvement from clearer exposition.
